subject: Cormorant Labs — on‑prem K8s provisioning, network & storage orchestration
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan@cormorantlabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onsite planning: hardware footprint & storage profile

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking our CTO through the options last week. We're ready to begin the on‑prem intake for the private cluster and wanted to get a planning workshop on the calendar. High level constraints from our side: 
- Site: Cormorant Labs HQ, NJ (3 racks available, single datacenter room)
- Workloads: model serving (low latency), batch fine‑tuning jobs, persistent vector DB for product search
- Compute footprint estimate: ~24 GPU nodes (8–10 GPUs/node spec), plus infra nodes for ingress/service mesh
- Storage: local NVMe on GPU nodes for model cache (~4 TB/node usable), plus a shared blockstore for stateful services and an archive NFS of ~100 TB for older tensors/archives
- Security: must integrate with our KMS (bring‑your‑own) and meet SOC2 audit requests (we'll need retention and access logs)
- Network: no direct internet routes for workloads; egress via a NAT gateway and strict egress filtering.

I've attached our current site inventory + a quick network diagram. Primary asks for the workshop: 
1) Recommended nodepool matrix (CPU/GPU/infra/storage) with failover/eviction guidance
2) Persistent volume strategy (local PV + replicated blockstore vs distributed storage like Ceph)
3) Network design constraints (BGP/NAT, MTU, VLAN plan) and any firewall/eBPF considerations
4) Compliance checklist we should prepare prior to the on‑site

Can you and your infra team propose 2–3 slot options for a 90‑minute workshop next week? Thanks — Evan

Head of Infrastructure

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Torres <evan@cormorantlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite planning: hardware footprint & storage profile

Thanks Evan — this is a great starting point. I've pulled together an initial operational proposal and a short pre‑work checklist so the workshop is productive. Summary/decisions we recommend before the session:

1) Cluster control plane and HA:
- 3 control plane VMs on the management VLAN (not colocated with GPU hosts) for quorum and etcd resilience.
- Use kubeadm/managed control plane pattern we ship for Private deployments; plan for regular etcd backups to the archive NFS.

2) Node pools (proposal):
- gpu-serving: 24 nodes, each with high‑memory host (12–16 vCPU, 512GB), 8 accelerator cards (local NVMe for model cache), tainted for inference pods.
- gpu-batch: 6–8 nodes (same HW family) unscheduled for latency critical traffic; autoscale via reserved burst pool for nightly fine‑tuning.
- infra: 3–5 nodes (smaller CPU‑heavy) for ingress, proxy/mesh, logging, and metrics collectors.
- storage-proxy: 3 nodes that run the CSI controller and act as gateway for the shared blockstore cluster.

3) Storage architecture:
- Local NVMe for hot model cache: use a local PV + NodeAffinity and a lightweight CSI (local static provisioning) so model processes get predictable IOPS.
- Durable blockstore: recommend Rook/Ceph for replicated block volumes if you want flexible snapshotting and replication within the rack. If operational simplicity is prioritized and the customer can accept per‑rack failure domain limits, Longhorn is acceptable for small clusters.
- Archive tier: NFS on a network appliance (100 TB), backed up nightly; use lifecycle policies to move older artifacts to air‑gapped cold storage.
- Encryption: all block volumes encrypted; integrate Redwood's KMS connector with your BYO KMS for envelope encryption keys. We'll need the KMS admin contact and role mapping for the integration.

4) Network & egress:
- CNI: use Calico with BGP peering to site fabric for pod routing; set MTU to match switch MTU (likely 9000).
- Egress: single NAT gateway cluster egress + egress policies on Calico to restrict outbound. Consider eBPF / Cilium for more granular L7 controls if you plan to enforce service‑level policies.
- Peering: control traffic between GPU rack and management VLAN via ACLs and dedicated VLANs for storage traffic to ensure isolation.

5) Observability & SLOs:
- We'll deploy per‑node token cost and latency tracers in the infra pool; please confirm whether you want sampling across pods or full tracing.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the KMS owner's email (we need an IAM principal for integration) and whether you have rack‑level BGP (yes/no)?
- Proposed workshop slots: May 6 14:00–15:30 ET, May 7 10:00–11:30 ET, May 10 16:00–17:30 ET.

I've attached a compact pre‑work checklist and our suggested nodepool matrix (spreadsheet). If we align on the storage backend choice (Rook/Ceph vs Longhorn) before the workshop we can run a short I/O baseline on your NVMe targets during the session.

Thanks — Kim

---
Kimberly Park
Principal Deployment Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Evan Torres <evan@cormorantlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite planning: hardware footprint & storage profile

Couple of notes from the networking and perf side:

- MTU & jumbo frames: confirm the switch fabric can sustain 9000 across the path; if there are any L2 devices that strip jumbo frames we'll default to 1500 to avoid fragmentation overhead.
- BGP: If you have spine/leaf BGP we should peer the Calico nodes directly and advertise pod CIDRs; otherwise we'll run a NAT ingress for services.
- Service mesh: for model telemetry and secure service‑to‑service TLS, we recommend a lightweight mesh (mTLS offload on the ingress) — but only if you can commit the extra CPU for sidecars on infra nodes.
- Storage QoS: for NVMe local, we need an IOPS baseline. I propose we run a fio profile during the workshop against a representative node (read/write mix for model loads). I'll bring a perf matrix to compare expected p95 latencies against local NVMe and Ceph RBD.

Attaching a short performance-matrix PDF that maps NVMe size/IOPS targets to expected GPU model load.

- Small operational ask: please confirm whether your facility team can provide remote KVM access to one GPU host for baseline testing during the workshop.

Jonas
Senior Systems Architect, Redwood Inference

Evan — thanks, and looping in a short preflight security checklist so your compliance team can start gathering items: 

- SOC2 evidence: retention windows, user access audit logs (we'll need 90 days by default), and network ACL logs.
- KMS: policy for key rotation and admin IAM principals (we'll need a service account that can perform Decrypt/Encrypt via your KMS).
- Audit access: confirm which SREs will need cross‑account read access to cluster logs; we'll provide a minimal role mapping template.
- Data flow diagram: please fill the attached diagram with where sensitive artifacts are generated and who consumes them (this speeds our checklist review).

I'll attach a SOC2 evidence request template and a short KMS integration primer. If you can provide the KMS admin contact and confirm the NAT egress box FQDN/IP range, we'll add those to the playbook.

Proposed workshop slot confirmed: May 6 14:00–15:30 ET (we'll send a calendar invite).

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
